hypothesis: attribute signal per direction is larger in historical generators
mathematical_basis: Gaussian-X Fisher per direction = eig(F'F)/sigma^2; Poisson-X: eig(sum_l lambda_il f_l f_l')
implementation_fact: historical rows fixed at ||f_l||^2 = 0.9 -> trace(F'F) = 13.5 for every K; canonical mean ||f_l||^2 = 0.5, equal singular values
csv_evidence: K=5 median X Fisher per direction: canonical 2.07 (n=75); early ExpFam Poisson 4.14; MATLAB/Python Gaussian 27.0; paper-text generator ~1500
verdict: SUPPORTED as a difference (2x Poisson-to-Poisson, 13x Gaussian)
remaining_confound: co-varies with Y signal, n, mask, Z normalisation and estimator

mathematical_basis: Y Fisher per direction ~ w^2 sum_j s(1-s) z_j z_j'
implementation_fact: MATLAB/Python w = 3 randn (K*=5 data: w = 5.03); early ExpFam w = 1.5; canonical w = sqrt(3/5) = 0.775 with 80% of pairs
csv_evidence: K=5 median Y Fisher per direction: canonical 5.1 (n=75); early ExpFam 32.1 (n=150); MATLAB/Python 105
remaining_confound: includes the n difference (Y Fisher ~ n)
falsifying_experiment: E5 (w alone); PR #155 C varied w x sqrt(1.8) at n=75

csv_evidence: historical_k_selection_summary.csv: Scenario A under-slack K*=5 median 1095, K*=9 236 (min 90)

remaining_confound: Scenario A also had historical F, w, n

hypothesis: Z / X normalisation changes the generating law
mathematical_basis: column z-score of Z fixes each column's sample variance; X z-score changes units only (Fisher invariant)
implementation_fact: MATLAB, Python, early ExpFam z-score Z; canonical does not
verdict: INCONCLUSIVE (not isolated; X z-score is information-neutral, Z z-score is not tested)
falsifying_experiment: E3 variant: canonical with and without Z standardisation

implementation_fact: paper Fig.3 implies -2lnL between 1.6 and 193 at k >= k* (scale incompatible with any repository Q2 score); Python and C_Q include ln p(Z): +425.7 per added dimension at n=150
